title: Egg White Tuna Scramble
subtitle: Pantry breakfast. 2 min prep, 4 min cook.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Tops carries CP and Allbest liquid egg-white bottles in the egg fridge. 1 cup ≈ 240ml ≈ 8 large whites.
Sealect or Roza, 'in water' or 'in spring water' — NOT in oil. Standard 165g can drains to ~130g.
ingredients.note: Drain hard — pressed against the lid, then a paper-towel squeeze.
Oil cap. Or use 1-second cooking spray.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Shark brand or Sriraja Panich (the original). Skip the American Huy Fong.

ingredients.note: Adds 10 kcal, 2g carbs. Worth it for colour.

substitutions.note: Sealect canned chicken — same shelf. Milder, less fishy mornings.
Richer, more satiating, drops protein to ~54g. Still in range.

steps.text: Drain tuna ruthlessly. Press against lid, then squeeze in paper towel. Flake into chunks.
Heat 1 tsp oil in non-stick pan, medium. Add tuna flakes, toast 60 sec until edges crisp.
Pour in egg whites. Don't stir for 20 sec — let the base set. Then push from edges to centre with spatula.
When most of the whites are set but still glossy (~90 sec total), kill heat. They'll finish in the pan.
Slide onto plate. Sriracha streak across. Top with spring onion, tomato, cilantro, pepper.

serves_with.note: +1 slice = ~80 kcal, 15g carbs, 4g protein. If you need carbs in the morning.

notes: This is the high-protein breakfast that works when you've got nothing in the fridge. Liquid egg whites + canned tuna are both 6-month pantry items. Sub goes the other way too: drained canned chicken if tuna tastes too fishy at 7am. Egg whites overcook in seconds — pull off heat when they look 80% done, residual heat takes them home.
